KB_001.title: Resetting Your SSO Password
KB_001.short_description: Self-service password reset for the SSO portal
KB_001.body: If your SSO password has expired or you are locked out: 1. Open the SSO portal login page and select "Forgot password". 2. Enter your corporate email address. 3. Approve the MFA prompt on your enrolled device. 4. Choose a new password that meets the policy shown on screen. 5. Wait five minutes before logging in to WMS so the change replicates. If you are still locked out after ten minutes, contact the Service Desk.

KB_002.title: VPN Client Setup and First Connection
KB_002.short_description: Installing and connecting the VPN client
KB_002.body: To set up VPN access on a company laptop: 1. Open the software portal and install "Westfield VPN Client". 2. Launch the client and sign in with your SSO credentials. 3. Approve the MFA prompt. 4. Select the "Corporate" profile and connect. The status icon turns green when the tunnel is up. Field staff at distribution centers should use the "Warehouse" profile instead - it routes WMS traffic directly.

KB_003.title: Troubleshooting VPN Disconnects
KB_003.body: For repeated VPN drops: 1. Confirm the client is on the current version (check the software portal). 2. Delete and re-import the connection profile. 3. Check home router MTU - values below 1400 cause tunnel resets. 4. Collect client logs (Help > Export Logs) and attach them to the ticket before escalating to IT Support L2.

KB_004.title: Mapping Departmental Network Shares
KB_004.body: Drive mappings are applied by the login script based on share-group membership. To grant a user access: 1. Confirm the request is approved by the share owner. 2. Add the user to the matching share group in the directory. 3. Have the user log out and back in. Manual mapping is discouraged - it bypasses the audit trail. If a mapping fails with a path error, verify the user's group membership first.

KB_005.title: Fixing Duplex Printing Jams
KB_005.body: When a printer jams only on double-sided jobs: 1. Power off and open the rear duplex unit. 2. Remove any jammed sheets and check the duplex rollers for wear (shiny, smooth surface means worn). 3. Clean the feed path with a lint-free cloth. 4. Run twenty duplex test pages. Replace the roller kit if jams persist - stock is held at each site.

KB_006.title: Reinstalling the WMS Client
KB_006.short_description: Clean reinstall procedure for the WMS client
KB_006.body: For persistent WMS client freezes or corrupt local state: 1. Export the user's local settings from the client if it opens. 2. Uninstall the client and delete the local cache folder. 3. Reinstall from the software portal. 4. Clear the local print queue cache before first launch. 5. Verify a test scan registers in WMS before returning the device to the floor.

KB_007.title: Pairing Barcode Scanners with WMS Tablets
KB_007.body: To pair a scanner: 1. Confirm the scanner firmware is current - re-flash from the field kit if unsure. 2. On the tablet, remove the old pairing entry. 3. Hold the scanner function key for five seconds to enter pairing mode. 4. Select the scanner on the tablet and scan the confirmation barcode. 5. Test with three item scans in WMS. Timeout errors during pairing usually mean stale firmware.

KB_008.title: Requesting Software Installation
KB_008.body: To request software: 1. Check the software portal first - approved titles install without a ticket. 2. For anything else, raise a request with the business justification. 3. Licensed software needs your manager's approval, which the Service Desk will route automatically. 4. Installation is scheduled after approval. Unapproved software must not be installed manually.

KB_009.title: New Starter IT Onboarding Checklist
KB_009.body: For each new starter, complete in order: 1. Directory account and SSO enrollment. 2. Mailbox creation and group memberships. 3. WMS role assignment matching the job profile. 4. Laptop from the spare pool, enrolled in endpoint management. 5. MFA enrollment on first login - schedule fifteen minutes with the starter. Target completion: two business days before start date.

Ask the user to restart their mail client; the mailbox appears within an hour. 3. Note the approval reference in the ticket before resolving. Temporary access (leave cover) should include an end date for removal.

KB_013.title: Collaboration tools
KB_013.short_description: Which collaboration tools to use internally and with partner teams
KB_013.body:
Westfield IT uses a core set of collaboration tools. When a partner uses something different, an alternate tool may work better.

_Product mentions are informational, not an endorsement._

## Messaging and video calls

**Slack** organizes conversation into channels; Westfield IT creates a channel for your project. Use **Zoom** for video calls.

- Partner not checking Slack? Use email.
- Blocked by firewall/security policy? Use email, or try Microsoft Teams.

## Sharing files

**Westfield Drive** stores spreadsheets, slides, and documents, shareable with the team without being public. Westfield IT can grant partner access.

- No access, or blocked by firewall/security policy? Share by email or try **Microsoft SharePoint**.

## Tracking project tasks

**Trello** organizes tasks into lists (backlog, in progress, in review, done); boards can be private or public. Alternatives: Airtable, Smartsheet.

- Not part of the partner's workflow? Track progress in sprint ceremonies or by email.
- Blocked by firewall/security policy? Use a whiteboard tool instead.

## Calendars

Use **Outlook Calendar** to schedule meetings. If a partner's tools aren't compatible, coordinate times by email, phone, or Slack.

## Development and documentation

**GitHub** stores code and project documents in a repository ("repo"), public by default. Use the wiki for reference material like design principles or a roadmap.

## Whiteboarding

**FigJam** (Figma) is the standard whiteboard, replacing Mural. Export important Mural boards as PDF before access is lost.

## Feedback collection

**Qualtrics** supports surveys and dashboards; request a license. Check with the security team before distributing outside the company.

## Setting up tools with partners

Before a project starts, the Account Manager should learn the partner's tools, confirm access to Westfield IT's tools, and resolve barriers early.

- **Meet partners where they are** — use their tool if it works.
- **Expect trial and error** — test tools in an early sprint.
- **Ask around** — post in Slack if a teammate's solved it before.

If a partner resists a tool, find out why — security, an approval process, or an existing alternative. Plan early for transferring documents, code, and accounts.

Help partners adopt tools with brief training, a low-risk trial space, and a short conventions doc. To offboard, help partners get their own accounts or equivalents for any tool used; the Account Manager handles removal and export with advance notice.

## Using partners' tools

It's fine to use a partner's own tool for their data; they own its security review. Only approved software may go on Westfield-issued machines — prefer a web-based version. If unsure, ask the security team.

KB_014.title: Distributed
KB_014.short_description: Guide for Westfield Logistics employees working remotely or distributed
KB_014.body:
Before you do anything, read our best practices for making distributed teams work.

## How do I...

### Set up my computer?
Employees receive a MacBook or PC and an iPhone or Android from Westfield Logistics; you may not get your work phone on day one.

Set your two-factor authentication (2FA) codes to deliver to your cell phone on day one — use your personal phone temporarily if your work phone hasn't arrived. **Without 2FA configured, you can't access email outside company offices.** See the Equipment article on the intranet for setup steps.

### Get a one-time password?
Set up a SecureAuth OTP application, or visit otp.westfieldlogistics.com.

### Visit another Westfield Logistics location?
Your access badge should work at other locations. Your manager or the Service Desk can request access to the Chicago, Dallas, or Portland buildings (a few days' turnaround). After the confirmation email, visit that location's security office to activate your badge.

### Connect to the network remotely?
See the Logging In & Networks article on the intranet.

### What supplies do remote employees receive?
Westfield Logistics provides a laptop and phone, not desk chairs or furniture. Westfield IT can send a remote kit — monitor, keyboard, mouse, headset, connectivity hub — pick what you need. Printers are available with additional justification.

### Advice from distributed colleagues
- Use a plug-in headset with a mic; laptop mics cause echo on calls.
- Need a wireless keyboard, mouse, or standing-desk gear? Ask on Slack — Westfield IT can help.
- Assume colleagues work asynchronously — document decisions in Slack, email, or Westfield Drive so they're searchable later.

## Keeping in touch
Over-communicate: others can't see you're "at work," so post updates and speak up on calls if you can't hear. IT applications team members should keep their Outlook Out of Office calendar current when working somewhere other than usual.

## Work-life balance
- Stop working once you've done a good day's work.
- Set yourself inactive on Slack and disable phone notifications when you're off for the day.
- Set boundaries early; block your working hours in Outlook Calendar.
- Meet people and join projects that interest you — grab a virtual coffee with colleagues over Zoom just to say hello.
- Stay active with walks, bike rides, or a standing desk, and get out to see other humans — Slack all day isn't a substitute for real interaction.

## Making a micropurchase

For guidance on requesting a micropurchase, see the instructions for your category:

- Business cards
- Conferences, events, and training
- Equipment
- Office supplies
- Services
- Software

### Business cards

We use business cards sparingly. If you need them for outreach or a specific meeting with partners, you can request standard Westfield Logistics business cards (no Westfield IT or IT applications team branding).

1. Go to the business card ordering site. Verify your email and create an account. Use a password you're comfortable sharing with the Westfield IT Ops team, since they'll need to log in as you to complete the purchase.
2. Fill in the required information, finalize your card design, and review your proof. Proceed to checkout, choose your quantity, and add the mailing address.
3. At the final checkout step (where credit card info is requested), request approval through the purchase request form. The Westfield IT Ops team reviews your order; once approved, they'll log into your account and make the payment. Cards arrive 7-10 business days later.

If you want Westfield IT or IT applications team branding, you must purchase your own cards, but get approval from the marketing/outreach team first.

### Office supplies

Check your warehouse or office supply room first. If what you need isn't available, submit the purchase request form. The Westfield IT Ops team decides whether to recommend approval by the Operations Director. Most office supplies can't be shipped to remote employees.

### Services

Examples of services procured this way:

- Engineering support
- Design services
- Compliance assessment services

For services under $10,000:

1. Submit the purchase request form to start the process; it outlines next steps.
2. For IT-related services, complete the open market justification form, attach it to the request, and include a vendor quote.
3. The procurement team reviews your request. Be ready to respond to questions or feedback promptly.
4. Once reviewed, the request goes through approval in the purchase request tracker. Your manager approves via a link emailed to them.
5. Once approved, the purchase card holder contacts you to complete the purchase.

KB_016.title: Sensitive information
KB_016.short_description: How to identify, categorize, and protect sensitive company information
KB_016.body:
Here's what you need to know about sensitive information at Westfield Logistics.

## What is considered sensitive?

Anything that could make our systems vulnerable or affect the privacy of others if it fell into the wrong hands. Examples include:

- passwords
- API keys
- private certificates and keys
- usernames
- email messages
- IP addresses, subnets, resource IDs, and account IDs
- non-public security vulnerabilities
- roles, policies, and group membership
- Personally Identifiable Information (PII)
- payment card industry (PCI) information
- personal health information (PHI)
- emergency procedures, such as evacuation plans

Westfield IT categorizes sensitive information as **secrets**, **privacy**, and **other** to guide how each type should be handled.

**Secrets** (passwords, API keys, private keys) must **never** be stored in source code repositories. Use an approved secret management solution instead.

**Privacy** information (PII, PHI) has its own handling guidance — check with the security team if you're unsure.

**Other** sensitive information (IP addresses, subnets, account IDs) may be kept in a private repository. IAM roles, policy names, and group names can be published as long as membership isn't attached — this helps deter spear phishing.

If you're unsure whether something is sensitive, ask the security team *before* sharing it. Don't post potentially sensitive information in Slack.

## What to do if you find or expose sensitive information

Report it immediately to the security team and follow the incident response process.

## Protecting Westfield systems

1. Install a pre-commit secret scanner (e.g., Caulking) so accidental API tokens or secrets are caught before they reach a repository.
2. **Never store sensitive information in source control**, including environment variables, private config, or PII. If credentials or config are pushed accidentally — even briefly — treat them as compromised: rotate them immediately, do not delete the commit, and follow the incident response process. Contact the Service Desk or the security team's Slack channel if you need help.
3. Follow standard build-pipeline security practices to protect secrets in CI/CD.

## Tools

Complete your annual Security Awareness and Privacy training, and only share sensitive information with people who need it and are authorized to see it.

### Westfield Drive

Use Westfield Drive to share sensitive files, spreadsheets, and documents, including PII of employees or the public. Share only with staff who have a direct need for the information.

### Password-protected files

You can password-protect a PDF or ZIP file. Send the encrypted file and the password to the recipient separately — ideally the password via phone call.

KB_017.title: Software Under $10,000
KB_017.short_description: How to request or install software purchases under $10,000
KB_017.body:
Need software to do your job? Follow these steps to access software Westfield Logistics already owns, or to request a purchase under $10,000. For purchases over $10,000, see Procurements Over $10,000.

Most software needs IT Standards approval before use. Exceptions:

- SaaS products where company data is not stored by the third party.
- Open source dependencies/libraries (npm, pip, gems, brew, etc.), when used as a component of a Westfield IT system already covered by a security review, or as general development packages — these are exempt from review.

If your software isn't covered by an exception, check whether it, or a similar approved product, already exists.

Note: the IT Operations team no longer procures software for business units due to staffing. It's your team's responsibility to confirm the vendor will meet Westfield's IT security requirements before you request the software — their upfront, good-faith cooperation with the security team is critical to approval.

Search the Approved Software Catalog to check if your software, or something similar, is already approved.

## Already-approved software

**Desktop software:**
1. Search the Westfield IT knowledge base (intranet.westfieldlogistics.com) for install instructions.
2. Check the Self Service app on your company-issued device — if listed, install it yourself.
3. If it's in neither, submit a Service Desk request to have it installed.

**SaaS:**
Approval doesn't guarantee an available license. If none are available, you and your manager will get an email saying the software must be purchased before use.
If you can't find software you believe is approved, or want alternatives with similar functionality, contact the Service Desk, or ask in the #it-software Slack channel.

## Software not yet approved

1. **Submit an IT Standards review request.** You'll get an email with the outcome and justification. Approved software is added to the Approved Software Catalog.
2. **Submit a Micropurchase request** if there's a cost involved, ideally at the same time. The Micropurchase team coordinates with the IT Standards team and runs the standard finance review alongside it.

## Considerations

- Vendor cooperation with the security team is required; if a vendor won't provide requested information, the tool can't be approved.
- SaaS approvals last one year. To continue past that, the vendor must maintain the required security certification, or the tool loses approval.

KB_018.title: Requirements for Passwords
KB_018.short_description: Steps for using a password manager and creating strong passwords.
KB_018.body:
Follow the steps below to create and maintain secure passwords.

## Requirements for passwords

As you set up your Westfield IT accounts and devices, follow three requirements: use a password manager, use unique passwords, and use strong passwords.

### 1. Use a password manager

Use a password manager so you only need to memorize a few strong passwords: your manager's master password, your laptop password and phone passcode, and maybe a few others, such as your iCloud password if that's your recovery method for a forgotten laptop password.

We recommend KeePassXC, which is open source and runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Install it from the Westfield Logistics Self-Service app. The KeePassXC database is stored locally on your computer; we recommend syncing it to Westfield Drive.

### 2. Use unique passwords

Use your password manager to generate a random, unique password for each service. macOS also has a built-in generator: in **Keychain Access**, go to **File > New Password Item** and click the key icon for suggestions.

Store security question answers in your password manager too. Instead of real answers (which someone with information about you could guess), use random nonsense answers and save them there.

Unique passwords matter even more than complex ones: if one service's password database is breached, attackers can't reuse that password on your other accounts. Use new passwords for work instead of reusing personal ones (don't reuse your Amazon password as your Westfield SSO password), and use a different password per service (don't reuse the same password for Slack and Westfield SSO).

### 3. Use strong passwords

You'll still need to memorize a few unique passwords, such as your password manager's master password. To resist guessing and "brute force" attacks:

- Avoid anything guessable by people who know you: birthdays, schools, pet names, favorite shows, and similar.
- Avoid common passwords: dictionary words, names of favorite people, pets, characters, or teams, and simple number-letter patterns are all frequently reused and easy to crack.
- Use longer passwords, since length makes brute forcing harder.

A good strategy: string together random words plus a few numbers, capital letters, or symbols. Or take a memorable line from a book, song, speech, or poem, and build a password from each word's first letter, adding capitalization, numbers, and symbols — or just use the whole line as your password. Pick a phrase nobody could guess from knowing you.

KB_019.title: Security incidents
KB_019.short_description: How to report security incidents, phishing, and suspicious activity
KB_019.body:
## Report IT security incidents or suspicious activity

An "incident" is a violation, or imminent threat of violation, of information security or privacy policies, acceptable use policies, or standard security practices.

If you notice unusual or suspicious activity on your computer, do not turn it off - this can destroy evidence. Report prohibited material, unauthorized programs, or misuse of Westfield Logistics systems to the Service Desk within 1 hour, with all available details.

Never share sensitive data via Slack or email. Westfield Drive is the only approved method for transmitting data during an active incident. If highly sensitive data is involved, don't attach it to your report - wait for instructions from the security team.

When in doubt, report it. False alarms and low-severity reports are welcome; they keep everyone practiced for when something serious happens.

## Reporting phishing

1. Don't click any links or delete the email yet.
2. Report it using the Cofense tool (fish icon) - see the Phishing Emails and Scams page on intranet.westfieldlogistics.com for instructions.
3. You may mark it spam/phishing only after reporting to Cofense (marking it first blocks Cofense from seeing it).
4. IT will triage and follow up if needed.

If you clicked a link, also email the Service Desk with "Security Incident" in the subject line and a brief description.

## Reporting other incidents

1. Within 1 hour of identifying an incident, email the Service Desk and the security team with "Security Incident" in the subject and a description (e.g., "credential committed to repo"), including relevant details and URLs. Do not delete or modify potential evidence.
2. Check your system's specific incident response plan, if one exists.
3. The security team will follow up with clarifying questions - e.g., which systems are affected and how quickly credentials can be rotated.

## For responders

Responders may spend up to 8 hours remediating an incident before worrying about billing - fix the problem first. Examples: sensitive data posted in a public Slack channel; a credential exposed in a code repository.

## Glossary

**Availability** - production systems running as expected; unexpected downtime is an incident.

**Confidentiality** - protection of secrets (PII, passwords, credentials, internal documents); report suspected leaks outside the company.

**Integrity** - soundness of systems and data; lost backups or deleted documents can signal a deeper incident.

## Contacts

Report incidents or ask questions via the Service Desk or your manager.

KB_020.title: Meetings and meeting tools

KB_021.title: Equipment
KB_021.short_description: Guide to receiving, setting up, and troubleshooting company-issued equipment
KB_021.body:
Westfield Logistics issues every employee a badge, laptop, and phone — laptops usually arrive first; phones may follow. The Onboarding Team submits your account request and ships gear to your home address on file.

- Encrypt any portable media you connect: right-click the drive, select Encrypt, set a strong password.

New hires get an iPhone via the Onboarding Team and IT Service Desk, shipped by UPS (signature required) with activation instructions.

**Rules:**
- Passcode over 14 characters, letters and numbers, known only to you.

- Set up MFA at otp.westfieldlogistics.com with your work/personal numbers; see the Slack/Outlook guides for authenticator or SMS setup.

Request a home office kit (monitor, keyboard, mouse, headset, hub) via an IT ticket. Wireless peripherals, printers, and other non-standard gear need manager/IT approval via an exception waiver. For a documented medical need, attach a doctor's note and contact the Service Desk.

## Passwords

See the guide on setting and managing passwords.

KB_022.title: Logging in & Networks
KB_022.short_description: Steps for SSO, Mac password, Citrix VDI, and network logins
KB_022.body:
This article covers best practices for logging into your company accounts and apps.

## Westfield SSO account

This is your account for signing into company systems, including your Outlook/Exchange email, Outlook Calendar, and Westfield Drive. Your account name follows the format `FirstnameMiddleinitialLastname` (e.g., `JohnASmith`). See the Service Desk's password guidance article for tips on choosing a secure password.

When you sign in while off the Westfield wireless network, you'll be asked whether "This is a public computer" or "This is a private computer." Always choose "This is a private computer" unless you're using a computer you don't own (e.g., a library computer).

### Changing your Westfield SSO password

Change your password immediately when you join Westfield Logistics, and every 90 days after that. Reset it through the Westfield SSO password reset tool. Lock and unlock your workstation (in-office or remote) afterward so the new password caches correctly.

Detailed reset steps: Knowledge Base article KB0022142.

## Changing or resetting your Macbook login password

If your local Mac password (not your SSO password) is due to expire within 14 days, you'll be prompted to change it. Steps: Knowledge Base article KB0024344.

Password requirements:
1. Changed every 90 days
2. Last 24 passwords can't be reused
3. Must be changed immediately if forgotten or compromised, regardless of age
4. Minimum 16 characters

## Logging into apps with your Westfield SSO account

Some apps let you sign in with your Westfield SSO account. Only grant "Basic Info" or "Limited Access to Data and Files" — broader access requires a Service Desk ticket. Contact the Service Desk to request expanded access or to check your current app permissions.

## Citrix (virtual desktop) login

Connect to your virtual desktop at vdi.westfieldlogistics.com. [See detailed instructions.]

## Connecting to Westfield networks

For on-site and remote network setup, see the connectivity guide at intranet.westfieldlogistics.com.

Having trouble connecting a Mac? Use the Westfield Guest Wi-Fi — see the same guide's "How to connect an Apple device" section.

---

Contact the Service Desk.

KB_023.title: Access badge
KB_023.short_description: How to get, activate, and use your access badge
KB_023.body:
_a.k.a. your "Smart Card" or "access badge"._

## Getting issued a badge

Your access badge gets you into Westfield Logistics buildings and skips security lines.

Even if you're based at one site, your badge can be permissioned for other locations (Chicago, Dallas, Portland) — contact the security team to start that, then visit the security office at each new building to activate your badge.

New badges are processed weekly. When ready, you'll get a pickup email with a temporary password — bring it with you. Contact the security team to check badge status.

## Using your badge with a company Mac

### Setup

Once you have your badge and PIN, contact the Service Desk to set up your computer for login (mention it's a MacBook).

1. Open the Self Service app, select "SmartCard/Badge," and find Smart Card Certificate Validation and Map Smartcard.
2. Plug in a card reader and insert your badge.
3. Click "Test" on Smart Card Certificate Validation. Contact the Service Desk if it doesn't validate.
4. Click "Install" on Map Smartcard and let it finish. Don't remove your card yet.
5. Remove your card and log out — do not reboot, this can brick the machine.

### Password vs. PIN

Company Macs require your badge to log in, so you'll use a PIN instead of your Westfield SSO password for most actions: login, unlocking your screen, running `sudo`, installing apps, changing System Preferences, and similar. Only the very first boot uses your Mac password.

If prompted to "reset your password," that's your local Mac password, not SSO or PIN — do it right away, since it times out.

### Certificate prompt

If asked to choose a certificate with your badge inserted, two will show your name — pick the first, or check the "Usage" field and choose the one that's only "Digital Signature." Picked wrong? Try again in an incognito window.

### Card readers

Since new Macs have only two USB-C ports, you'll likely need a dongle for a spare port. If the dongle can't power the reader, plug the reader directly into the computer instead and route power through the dongle.

### Issues

- **Lost badge**: contact the security team immediately.
- **Unreliable reader**: request a backup from the Service Desk.
- **"Certificate not trusted" error**: clean the badge's contact pad with a pencil eraser, wipe off debris, and reinsert.
- **Forgot your badge**: contact the Service Desk — they can temporarily enable username/password login remotely.

KB_025.title: Docusign
KB_025.short_description: How to use DocuSign templates and submit support tickets
KB_025.body:
Westfield Logistics provides access to DocuSign so employees can sign and request signatures on documents.

## Use DocuSign templates to complete forms

Westfield Logistics has set up shared templates in DocuSign for certain HR forms, with automatic email routing to get the right signatures.

Forms with DocuSign templates include:

- Leave Donation Program
- Paid Parental Leave (PPL)

4. Enter the name of the form or program in the search bar.

KB_026.title: Outlook Email
KB_026.short_description: How to access, manage, and customize your Outlook corporate email account.
KB_026.body:
We use Outlook and Exchange for corporate email.

## Usage

You can access your email through Outlook on the web or the Outlook desktop and mobile apps.

## Tips

- **For basic Outlook tips and best practices**, check out the Email with Outlook page on the intranet (intranet.westfieldlogistics.com).

- **Enable clickable `mailto:` links in Chrome**:

KB_027.title: Outlook Calendar
KB_027.short_description: How to use, configure, and share your Outlook Calendar
KB_027.body:
Outlook Calendar is a web-based calendar that gives us a single point of reference for scheduling time.

## Setup

Outlook Calendar is a web application, so there's no installation necessary.

## Usage

Westfield IT uses **shared calendars** for events, interviews, and "out of office" time, as well as for working groups, guilds, and blog planning.

Shared calendars for internal communication:

- **Westfield IT Classes** — new hire and skills-based training sessions.
- **Westfield IT Guilds and Working Groups** — meetings and events for working groups and guilds.
- **Westfield IT Solutions Events** — events hosted by the Solutions team.

To subscribe to a shared calendar, open its link and use **Add calendar > Subscribe from web** in Outlook Calendar.

## Tips

- Add Zoom links to your calendar invites.
- Specify your working hours.
- View the availability of other Westfield Logistics employees when scheduling meetings.
- You can share specific event invites with external parties, but you can't share unrestricted access to your entire calendar outside Westfield Logistics.
- View multiple time zones at once.

### Change default event duration

The default event duration is 30 minutes. To change it:

1. Open **Settings**.
2. Under **General > Event Settings**, choose 15, 30, 60, 90, or 120 minutes.
3. For shorter meetings, select **Speedy meetings**: 30-minute meetings become 25, 60 become 50, 90 become 80, and 120 become 110.
4. Click **Save**.

### Change default event permissions

By default, guests can't modify events they're invited to. To allow more flexible invitations:

1. Open **Settings**.
2. Under **General > Event Settings**, choose **Default guest permissions**.
3. Select your desired default guest permissions.

### Sync with your iPhone

Sync your schedule to an iOS device using the Outlook app, signing in with your Outlook/Exchange account.

### Share your calendar outside Westfield Logistics

You can't share full calendar access outside Westfield Logistics, but you can share your free/busy times — useful for partners or personal calendars.

1. Click the three dots next to the calendar you want to share, then choose **Settings and sharing**.
2. Under **Access permissions for events**, check **Make available to public**, select **See only free/busy (hide details)**, and copy the shareable link. Open it in a private/incognito browser tab to preview it as an outsider would see it.
3. To add your work calendar to a personal calendar, scroll to **Share with specific people or groups**, enter the email account, and select **See only free/busy (hide details)**.

KB_028.title: Westfield Drive
KB_028.short_description: How to share, organize, and secure files in Westfield Drive
KB_028.body:
Westfield Drive is a cloud storage and file backup system used to organize project work and templates, and to collaborate on documents, presentations, and spreadsheets. No installation is required to use it in a browser.

## Permissions and sharing

1. Share files with your whole team by adding your team's distribution list to the share list. Select "do not notify" if you don't need to flag it immediately.
2. You can share with any Westfield Logistics employee, but don't default to sharing with the entire company. IT will adjust permissions that are too open, and files containing sensitive information may be blocked automatically.
3. You can share whole folders; new files added to a shared folder automatically inherit its sharing settings.
4. Most departments keep a shared team folder in Westfield Drive for collaboration.
5. Files can't be published to the web or shared with the public — sharing is limited to Westfield Logistics employees or specific invited users.
6. If an external partner needs file access, contact the Service Desk about setting up an external sharing account. Files that partner creates through that account fall outside Westfield Logistics's compliance boundary.

## Usage

- Follow the Westfield Logistics Code of Conduct; report violations through the standard reporting process.
- Always use your Westfield SSO account, not a personal account, especially when working with outside partners. Official company documents must stay in your Westfield Drive account for compliance reasons.

## Tips

- Shift+Z adds a file or folder to multiple locations at once — useful for organizing documents more than one way.
- To find recently opened documents, use the "Last opened by me" view.
- Star or "Add to My Drive" items you use often for quick access.
- Search covers everything shared with you, not just your own files.
- If a folder looks empty, refresh your browser a few times.

## Security

If a non-Westfield service asks to access your Westfield Drive account (for example, to enable an integration), deny the request — don't grant third-party apps access to Westfield Drive. To check, review your account's list of connected apps for anything with Drive access.

## Local editing

A desktop sync app is available for local editing of files stored in Westfield Drive. If you get a "can't load" error, try clearing your browser cache.

## API access

To request access to Westfield Drive APIs, submit a request to Westfield IT describing what you're building. Access may be restricted based on the data sensitivity classification of the requesting system.

KB_029.title: Distribution Lists
KB_029.short_description: Request, manage, and configure Westfield email distribution lists
KB_029.body:
We use distribution lists to manage team and interest-based email groups. A list of distribution lists Westfield IT maintains is available on the [intranet](https://intranet.westfieldlogistics.com).

## Request a distribution list

Submit a request through the Service Desk portal. Search for "distribution list" and complete the creation request form.

## Manage a distribution list

To find the lists you belong to, or manage lists where you're an owner, contact the Service Desk or use the distribution list settings in Outlook.

## How are Westfield distribution lists different from public lists?

Westfield distribution lists work a little differently than public mailing lists. People outside Westfield can't join a Westfield list directly, but can still receive email if added as an external contact. Likewise, you can't join a public mailing list with your Westfield email through its normal signup process, but you can still receive messages if you're added directly.

If you regularly need to include people outside Westfield, a listserv may be a better fit. If a suitable external list already exists, consider joining that one instead.

## How do I add external members to my list?

To let people outside Westfield join your list, contact the Service Desk and ask them to enable:

- External members allowed
- Email posting enabled

When adding external contacts, use **add** rather than **invite** — you'll need to manage their notification settings (like daily digests) on their behalf.

## How can my list receive email from anyone?

To let anyone send email to your list, not just members, ask the Service Desk to enable:

- Posting from anyone (not just members)
- Email posting enabled

## Tips

- Replies you send from the list will come from your personal Outlook account, not the list address. If you're a list owner, you can select the list's address when composing a reply.

KB_030.title: HR Links
KB_030.short_description: Guide to submitting timesheets, leave requests, and overtime in HR Links
KB_030.body:
HR Links is Westfield Logistics' system for timesheets, leave, schedules, benefits, telework agreements, performance reviews, personal info, and 401(k) contributions. Supervisors also use it for approvals and reports. Guides and the leave-type comparison chart are on the intranet.

## Submitting your timesheet

Submit your timesheet at the end of each biweekly pay period; confirm timing with your supervisor. Submit before going on leave — for an unplanned absence, your supervisor can submit for you. See the intranet guide "Creating a Timesheet."

- After selecting **Employee Timesheet**, select **Yes** if asked to apply your schedule.
- **Needs Approval** = submitted successfully. **No Timesheet** = not yet submitted.
- Resubmit corrections as needed before your supervisor's deadline; after the period closes, ask your supervisor to approve any changes.

## Using leave

Submit an absence request at least 3 business days ahead (see the comparison chart for leave codes); edit promptly if plans change, or contact your supervisor if unplanned.

- One request covers back-to-back full days; use separate requests for non-consecutive days, or partial days with different hours.
- Edit a request to change hours, or cancel it to remove leave entirely.
- Error "overlapping with an existing absence": edit your canceled request instead of creating a new one, or contact the Service Desk.
- If leave affects a timesheet already submitted, manually adjust the hours (e.g., Regular Time) and resubmit. For a past pay period, ask your supervisor to amend it.
- Advanced annual/sick leave: request like normal leave. HR Links flags an error, cleared by your supervisor's comment-box approval. Advanced sick leave needs paperwork first; temporary employees can't borrow more than they'll earn before their contract ends.
- Paid parental leave: once approved, select **Paid Parental Lv Birth Balance** and submit like any request.

## Overtime, comp time, and credit hours

1. Submit the request in HR Links for supervisor approval.
2. Once approved, manually add the hours to your timesheet on the day(s) earned — HR Links doesn't link them automatically.

Use earned hours later via a normal leave request.

## Checking your information

- **FLSA overtime status**: View My HR Information > Position Data > FLSA Status.
- **Award leave expiration**: one year after the effective date on your personnel record.
- **Temporary employee contract end date**: View My Employment Information > Employment Data 1.

For timesheet reports, see the intranet guide "Pulling a Timesheet Report." Contact the Service Desk for help.

KB_031.title: Microsoft Office
KB_031.short_description: How to request a temporary or installed Microsoft Office license
KB_031.body:

KB_032.title: Sharing calendars with partners
KB_032.short_description: How to share Outlook calendars both ways with external partners
KB_032.body:
If you're running a project with a partner company, having visibility into team members' calendars makes scheduling meetings easier so you know when people are available.

At Westfield Logistics we can readily view each other's personal calendars (or at least free/busy status) and team calendars in Outlook Calendar. Partners at other organizations may have different IT policies and settings, so sharing calendars both ways can take more effort. It's usually possible, though. Here's how:

## Share your Outlook Calendar directly with a partner

1. In Outlook Calendar, select the calendar you want to share, then choose the sharing/permissions option for that calendar.
2. Set the appropriate access level: see only free/busy time, or see full event details. Note: personal calendars at Westfield Logistics are typically limited to free/busy visibility only.
3. Generate a shareable calendar link and send it to your partner.
4. Ask your partner to add that link as an internet/subscribed calendar in whatever calendar program they use.
5. Confirm your partner can see your events, and that updates (new or changed events) also show up for them.
6. If that works, ask your partner to share their calendar back with you the same way:
   - Partners using Outlook can follow the same steps above.
   - Partners using another calendar tool should check that tool's documentation for sharing a calendar link.
7. Import your partner's calendar link into your Outlook Calendar and confirm you can view their events, including updates.

If this doesn't work for your team, contact the Service Desk for other options.

KB_034.title: External collaboration through Slack
KB_034.short_description: How to add partners and public guests to Westfield Logistics Slack
KB_034.body:
Collaboration with people outside Westfield Logistics falls into two categories: partners on Slack, and the public.

## Working with partners on Slack

Partners include:

- Organizations working with Westfield IT under a formal partnership agreement
- Vendors under contract (not just a Terms of Service) with Westfield IT
- Vendors working with Westfield Logistics on a joint project under a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU)

This excludes the general public (who have their own channels) and unaffiliated partner-organization contacts.

Procurement sets a contractor's access level. Contractors embedded full-time or near-full-time with Westfield IT get full membership via their Westfield SSO email; others should be added as single- or multi-channel guests.

To add external collaborators or change channel sharing, submit a Service Desk ticket for a **Slack platform change** (covers Slack Connect and multi-channel guest requests). Use the "Add Slack guest member" ticket only for guests with a Westfield-managed account. Ask the Service Desk if unsure which to use.

Other Westfield Logistics employees (e.g., IT leadership) may also be added as full members, with your manager's approval.

### Dedicated channels

1. Create a `-partners` channel if an existing one doesn't fit.
2. Add partners via Slack Connect (preferred) or individually through a Slack platform change ticket.

### Shared channels

- **Multi-workspace channels** share a channel across Westfield Logistics' Slack Enterprise Grid.
- **Slack Connect** shares a channel with outside partners; request via a Slack platform change ticket. Preferred over guest access — it offloads user management to the partner and keeps their history searchable in their own workspace.

Shared channels follow the same content and retention rules as any other channel.

## Collaborating with the public

Westfield Logistics runs `-public` channels open to anyone. External partners not on a project can still be invited as guests. Request this, or a new public channel, via a Slack platform change ticket.

Treat public channels like a livestream or open meeting: don't post non-public materials there — publish them on a company website and link to them instead. Members of the public must follow the company Code of Conduct.

## Archive a channel

Archive a channel once a partner project ends: Slack Connect channels (double-diamond icon) require a Service Desk request; other channels can be archived by any member.

## Other Slack workspaces

You may join Slack workspaces run by partner organizations or contracted vendors using your Westfield SSO email; use a personal email address if invited in a personal capacity.

KB_035.title: Getting started with Slack
KB_035.short_description: How to access Slack, set up your profile, and use it responsibly
KB_035.body:
_Back to Slack page_

## What is Slack?

Slack is the messaging app Westfield Logistics uses for daily communication: join channels for group topics, or message individuals and small groups directly. Slack also has a call feature called "Huddles."

## How do I access Slack?

1. Go to the Westfield Logistics Slack workspace (linked from intranet.westfieldlogistics.com).
2. Sign in with your Westfield corporate email address.
3. Enter your Westfield SSO account credentials; complete MFA at otp.westfieldlogistics.com if asked.
4. You'll land in the company's default channel.

Desktop apps are available for Mac and Windows; mobile apps for your work phone are in the Apple/Google Play store.

## Do all employees have access?

Yes — new hires get full Slack access during onboarding.

## Do all teams use Slack the same way?

No. Each team sets its own norms (some use Huddles for standups, others stay text-only); ask your manager or onboarding buddy about yours. Slack also hosts informal "water cooler" chat — ask the Service Desk for the channel list.

## Is Slack content a company record?

Yes. Slack messages are business records, like email or documents, subject to legal discovery and retention policy. Treat Slack as semi-public — don't post anything you wouldn't want attributed back to you. Never post sensitive information; check with the security team for alternatives.

## How do I set up my profile?

Complete these fields after logging in:

- **Full Name, Time Zone, Email** — automatic, from your Westfield account.
- **Display Name** (required, editable anytime) — shown when teammates mention you.
- **Title, Name Pronunciation, Photo** (recommended).
- **Phone, Location, Personal README** (optional) — the README describes how you like to work and communicate.

Save and review your profile after editing.

## How do I use Slack responsibly?

- Westfield expects a safe, harassment-free culture on Slack; discuss norms with your manager.
- Tone is hard to convey in text — give constructive feedback privately, over Zoom or a call. Watch for "pile-ons": if a thread escalates, move it to Zoom.
- Share challenges and useful resources with your team.
- Don't post anything that could compromise system security or others' privacy.
- Flag inappropriate messages directly, with your manager, or with HR.
- Ask questions in the relevant channels; try another channel (email, Zoom, calendar invite) if a message goes unanswered for days.
- Ask your manager if anything here is unclear.

KB_036.title: Slack channel usage and best practices
KB_036.short_description: How to find, join, and understand Slack channel types
KB_036.body:
## What is a Slack channel?

When you log into the Westfield IT Slack, you're logging into the Westfield IT workspace. Under the workspace are multiple channels, which are how conversations are organized and where communication and collaboration take place.

A channel is a distinct place for a team to share messages, tools, and files. Each channel has a specific focus. Inside a channel, you'll find messages and threads that allow for organized, focused conversations.

## Is channel content viewable by everyone?

There are two types of channels — public and private.

Conversations and content in _public_ channels are searchable and viewable by anyone in the Westfield IT Slack. Public channels have a # symbol in front of the name.

Conversations and content in _private_ channels can be accessed only by members of that channel, and are searchable only by those members. Private channels have a 🔒 symbol in front of the name. Note: private channel content and direct messages may still be retrieved during legal or compliance reviews.

Slack also includes a Connect feature that creates shared channels between two Slack workspaces, so members of both can participate. Connect channels show a visual indicator above the message box noting that people from another workspace are present.

## How are channels created?

Channels can be created and named however your team organizes its work — by project, team, or office, among others.

## Will I create channels as I onboard?

As you onboard, your manager will add you to your team's channels. The onboarding team will also add you to a channel dedicated to onboarding questions. Your buddy and teammates may add you to other channels, and you can review the list of non-project channels to join.

Once you're more familiar with Slack, you can create your own channels later.

## Can I join other channels of interest?

Yes — review the list of non-project channels to join.

## Channel name prefixes and suffixes

| Prefix/suffix | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `admins-` | Administrators for various tools; used to request Slack invites, rename channels, etc. |
| `-partner` | Channels that include partners from other organizations. |
| `-public` | Channels that include members of the public. |
| `-shared` | Channels linked with another Slack org (via Connect). |
| `wg-` | Working groups. |
| `g-` | Guilds. |

Feel free to join any of these channels even if you're not an active member of the group — being interested is enough.

KB_037.title: Slack communication and notification best practices
KB_037.short_description: How to use Slack mentions, DMs, threads, and notifications effectively
KB_037.body:
_Back to Slack page_

## What are some communication best practices for Slack?

### @Mentions

To make sure someone sees a message, type @ followed by their name to mention them. This works even in channels they aren't in — Slack will offer to notify them.

### Direct messages

You can send a direct message (DM) to one person or a group. Note: DMs are subject to Westfield Logistics' records retention policy and may be reviewed by the security team or legal counsel.

### Editing messages

You can edit a message for 5 minutes after posting. You can't delete a message — instead, edit the text and add a note like "wrong channel." After 5 minutes, messages can no longer be edited or deleted.

Contact the security team to request deletion of a Slack message in the event of a security or personally identifiable information (PII) issue.

### Slack statuses

Set a status to show your availability next to your name — for example, an OOO emoji with "OOO until Monday 3/1."

### Threading

Use threads to reply to a specific post. Threads keep conversations grouped, notify only participants on new replies, and avoid extra notifications in the main channel after the initial post.

### Sharing a lot of information at once

Use posts to share large chunks of text.

### @here and @channel notifications

@channel and @here notify everyone in a channel. Use these sparingly, and only in channels for your specific team or project — set team guidelines on when to use them. For non-urgent updates, email channel members or pin a post instead.

## Avoiding Slack overload

You don't have to be part of every conversation — join and leave public channels as needed. Check with your manager before leaving a channel dedicated to your team. Leaving a private channel means a current member must re-add you.

Use Slack's search to find specific channels or conversations (e.g., searching for a benefits plan name).

### Setting a "not working" status

Set your status to _Away_ when you're off the clock or heads-down. You can also set a notification schedule so Slack shows you as offline outside certain hours.

### Managing notifications

Set notification preferences to control what triggers an alert, and pause notifications when you need to focus. You can turn off mobile notifications entirely — there's no expectation to respond outside your working hours.

KB_038.title: Slack user management, administration and security
KB_038.short_description: Admin guide for managing and offboarding Westfield Slack accounts
KB_038.body:
_Back to Slack page_

This page overviews the administrative tasks done to manage our Slack accounts at Westfield Logistics.

## Adding Westfield IT staff

The PeopleOps team will fill out a user request ticket for employees when they join Westfield IT.

## Offboarding

Slack users need to be offboarded in the following situations:

- Someone leaving Westfield Logistics
- A partner whose employment/engagement is ending
- A contractor who is no longer supporting Westfield IT

In all of these cases, the person's manager or engagement manager should **fill out a user modification ticket**.

An admin will then do one of the following:

- **Convert them to a Single-Channel Guest.**

  - Put them in one of the following channels (as appropriate):

    - The alumni channel (former full-time staff only, but treated as a public channel)
    - One of the `-public` channels (their pick)

  - Disable their 2FA.

    - ...unless you know they were using their personal device for 2FA — we don't want them to be locked out.

  - Change their email to their personal address.

  **NOTE:** When a Slack user is converted to a Single-Channel Guest, they keep access to their direct-message chat history but can't search for or start new direct messages with people they've never messaged before. Unless another channel is specified, the only channel that will still be accessible is #alumni.

- **Deactivate their account.**

If they were a partner, the admin will also set their `Downgraded/disabled on` date in the user request spreadsheet.

## Slack admins

Here are the resources used by Slack Admins to track and manage Slack accounts:

- Westfield IT's Slack administration guide
- Westfield IT's Slack ServiceNow tickets
- Delegation of admin responsibilities

## Security

Westfield Logistics' Slack Enterprise Grid deployment has been reviewed and approved by the security team.

KB_039.title: Trello
KB_039.short_description: Trello is being decommissioned; export your data and pick a replacement
KB_039.body:
## Trello decommission notice

Westfield IT has decommissioned Trello company-wide, effective September 1, 2025. After that date, your Trello boards and cards will no longer be accessible. If you have Trello content you need to keep, export it now.

- **Export format:** Use JSON to preserve full board content, including comments. CSV exports do not include comments. Follow Westfield IT's export instructions before your boards are removed.

Westfield IT has not designated a single replacement product. Consider these alternatives based on how you used Trello:

- **GitHub Projects** — Advanced project and issue tracking for technical teams; Kanban boards, automation, and developer workflow integration.
- **AppSheet Kanban** — Simple, visual Kanban app for teams who need drag-and-drop boards.
- **AppSheet Project Tracker** — Spreadsheet-style project tracker for timelines and status reporting.
- **Slack List** — Lightweight task lists inside Slack for teams that primarily collaborate there.
- **Microsoft OneNote** — Quick notes and simple checklists across devices.
- **Microsoft To Do** — Basic to-do lists integrated with Outlook email and Calendar for personal task tracking.

If you're unsure which tool to choose, discuss options with your team and your manager. Consider data retention, records requirements, and partner access when picking a replacement.

KB_040.title: Citrix
KB_040.short_description: How to install, log into, and use the Citrix VDI client
KB_040.body:
Citrix is a Windows virtual desktop client used to reach the Westfield Logistics intranet or test something in Internet Explorer.

## Setup

To launch Citrix, the Citrix Workspace App must be installed on your device. Company-issued Windows laptops already have it installed.

On a personal or non-standard device, install the Citrix Workspace App from Citrix's website (available for Windows and Mac) before continuing.

## Logging into the Citrix VDI

1. Go to vdi.westfieldlogistics.com to access the Citrix VDI.
   - To launch individual apps (such as Chrome or Internet Explorer) instead of the full virtual desktop, go to apps.westfieldlogistics.com.
2. Go to otp.westfieldlogistics.com and enter your Westfield SSO account info to get a Tokencode.
   - You can also generate a Tokencode with a one-time-password authenticator app on your phone — see the "Get a one-time password" article for setup.
3. Enter your Westfield SSO account info and the Tokencode on the Citrix login screen.

### First time connecting from a web browser

1. If prompted with a "Welcome to Citrix" window, select `Detect Receiver`.
2. When prompted to open in Citrix Workspace Launcher, click `Cancel`.
3. Click the `Already Installed` link.
4. Click the monitor icon for the VDI desktop you want to launch (available desktops vary by person).
5. A file will download in your browser. Click the `^` next to the file name and select "Always open files of this type."
6. Click the monitor icon again to launch the desktop. Future launches will skip the download step.

## Usage

See the Citrix page on the intranet for more detail.

## Software

Citrix is the easiest way to use Windows-only software on a Mac. If software you need isn't pre-installed, request it from the Service Desk.

On the request form, set "Where is the Software going to be installed?" to `VDI`, and "Enter VDI or Citrix here" to `Standard Desktop`.

## Tips

- To move files between your laptop and your Citrix desktop, use Westfield Drive. Use Chrome inside the Citrix desktop to download and upload files.

---

#### Still have questions?

Ask in Slack or contact the Service Desk.

KB_041.title: Zoom
KB_041.short_description: How to set up and use Zoom for company meetings
KB_041.body:
Westfield Logistics provides Zoom for employee use.

## Setup

1. Install the Zoom application through Self Service.
2. Click **Sign in with SSO**.
3. Enter `westfieldlogistics` as the company domain. If it's set to `.zoom.us` instead, click **I don't know the company domain** and enter your Westfield email address.
4. Consider adding a profile picture and your location and pronouns to your display name.

## How to host a meeting

General instructions. See the internal handbook guidance on hosting accessible meetings to help ensure everyone can fully participate.

### For meetings longer than 40 minutes

Check your Zoom profile to see your user type and meeting time limit. If you need to host meetings longer than 40 minutes, submit a request to the Service Desk to be upgraded to a Licensed user.

## Rules

- Only your Westfield SSO account may be used to host Zoom meetings you initiate.
- You may join Zoom meetings hosted by external partners, unless doing so requires accepting Zoom's Terms of Service or installing additional software.
- Meetings hosted by external partners should be limited to non-sensitive discussions.
- All Zoom meetings hosted by Westfield require a meeting password.
- Do not use a Personal Meeting ID (PMI) for meetings you host.
- Do not share Zoom meeting links on public social media; send links directly to invitees.
- For public meetings, limit screen sharing to Host Only.
